text:
anya: Heads-up — eu-west2 egress tail latency spiked ~3x over the last 30m. Observable correlates to sustained KV and embedding traffic from a couple of tenants.
sam: Which tenants? any noisy neighbor signature? :thinking_face:
dmitri: I see two high-throughput flows: tenant-42 (batch reranks) and tenant-omega (long embeddings fanout). KV eviction churn + socket backlog looks correlated.
anya: tenant-42 is running lots of small sequential requests, tenant-omega is a single client hammering embeddings-ish RPCs. Both hair-trigger our NIC queues at rack egress.
emily: Can we soft-cordon their egress at the ToR level and route them through a dedicated egress gateway (lower contention) for a short window? That would be non-disruptive if fallback is configured.
sam: Technically yes, but routing change requires a quick ACL update and a dedicated pool with matching CUDA profile. We also need leader approval for dedicated carveout (cost).
infra-bot: Runbook link: https://runbooks.redwood.internal/egress-cordon — recommended steps: identify flows, update egress ACL, shift to dedicated pool, monitor telemetry for 15m.
dmitri: Proposed quick plan:
1) Create temporary dedicated slice with 2x p4d equivalent capacity in eu-west2.
2) Update allocator labels for tenant-42/tenant-omega to prefer dedicated slice.
3) Apply ToR egress ACL to steer traffic to dedicated egress gateway.
4) Monitor p50/p95/p99 and NIC tx drops for 20m; rollback if error > 5%.
sam: I can spin the slice, ETA ~12m. Cost estimate: ~€65/hr for the temporary slice at current pricing, likely < €500 for the window if we run 6–8 hours.
anya: Sounds fine. Main ask: make sure we don't accidentally break cross-az placement for tenant-omega (their requests span two regions and may have affinity expectations).
emily: We'll add a sticky affinity rule for the dedicated slice so warm pools remain in-eu-west2 only. Also enable prefix KV caching on tenant-omega to reduce repeated embedding hits.
dmitri: Quick commands I'm going to run (dry-run first):

```
# create slice
infractl slice create --region eu-west2 --profile p4d-2x --name temp-egress-slice-1866 --duration 8h
# label tenants
infractl tenant update tenant-42 --alloc-preference slice=temp-egress-slice-1866
infractl tenant update tenant-omega --alloc-preference slice=temp-egress-slice-1866
# apply ToR egress ACL
netctl acl apply --tor rack-17 --policy cordon-egress-temp
```

sam: ping me before you apply the ACL so I can validate the BGP prep on the gateway.
anya: Will do. Also add a ticket for finance (temp slice billing) so CostOps is aware.
emily: I'll add an alert rule to mute the noisy-alert for 30m to avoid noiseflood, but keep page if p99 > 2s.
infra-bot: Allocator telemetry: https://telemetry.redwood.internal/allocs?slice=temp-egress-slice-1866 — enables live p50/p95 graphs.
dmitri: After 20m of stable metrics we'll document the config and consider a policy: auto-evict heavy egress tenants into a paid-dedicated-tier if they exceed sustained egress threshold for 30m.
sam: Agreed. Also follow-up: we should test NIC queue shaping on a canary rack to avoid carving expensive slices every time.
anya: OK starting step 1 now (create slice). I'll post back with timestamps. Thanks all :)
